ops.value: In Lê's published conversation with Land of January 2026, Lê states that capital is “a vastly more general intelligence than us humans”, that Kurzweil's 2040s prediction for AGI or the singularity and a “2027 thesis” are “both too late” (“Their dates should really be centuries ago”), and that LLMs are to capital as a species is to natural selection; Land calls this “a really good way of structuring this” and says “the natural selection mechanism is ultimately the intelligent mechanism”.

An interview transcript published by the interviewer. The proposition is stated in Lê's words; Land's words endorse Lê's comparison and speak of natural selection, not of capital by name. Lê's passage calling capital 'a vastly more general intelligence' does not itself say artificial or machine; the record rests on his setting capital against the AGI and singularity forecasts he names in the same turn. Not evidence that the comparison is sound.

ops.value: bears_on_proposition

The post does not call capitalism or the 'new plane of intelligence' artificial or machine intelligence, and does not state that machine intelligence assembles itself through capitalism; its passage on machines evolving themselves does not mention intelligence.

The Hyperstition post “Critique of Transcendental Miserablism” of 2007, signed “Old Nick”, states that capitalism “has consumed life and biological intelligence to create a new life and a new plane of intelligence, vast beyond human anticipation”. In a separate passage it states that machines, “incarnating market mechanics”, are “evolving themselves by quasi-darwinian alogorithms”.

ops.value: Earliest located W06 articulation with a dated wording: Land's remarks at the Incredible Machines conference (delivered 8 March 2014; transcript posted 10 March 2014), 'the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence'. The Hyperstition post 'Critique of Transcendental Miserablism' (15 January 2007, signed 'Old Nick'; title matches a Fanged Noumena chapter by Land) is recorded as bearing on W06: it speaks of capitalism creating 'a new plane of intelligence' but does not call that intelligence machine or artificial. Correction, 2026-10-31: the 2007 post was previously given the earliest-located role. 'Meltdown' articulates W06 but is read only in an undated CCRU web copy (the CCRU dates Abstract Culture swarm 1 'Winter, 1997'), so it cannot be earliest located. 'Circuitries' (1992) bears on W06. Lê's post of 2026 dates 'Machinic Desire' to 1993 and quotes a W06 passage from it ('an invasion from the future by an artificial intelligent space'); the essay itself (Textual Practice, 1993; Fanged Noumena, 2011) was not retrievable in a copy by the author or publisher. If it is read, it is likely to become the earliest located W06 text. Contesting: Negarestani and Mackay (2018) is the earliest located; jacob (2026) is later.
